headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty fell for the sixth straight week amid high oil prices and US Fed triggers.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Elevated crude oil prices continued to put pressure on Indian equities.
Concerns around US Fed policy decisions weighed on global sentiment.
Sustained Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) selling contributed to the weekly market drop.
Uncertainty around Tata Sons triggers and US H-1B visa policy scrutiny dampened investor confidence.
whatHappening: Sensex and NIFTY50 ended lower for the sixth consecutive week during the last trading session.
NTPC terminated a ₹413 crore BESS contract due to non-performance by the contractor.
Paytm remained in focus amid broader market volatility and trading outlook.
Investors are tracking support levels for Sensex and Nifty as trading resumes next week.

summary:
In the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty fell to wrap up their sixth consecutive week of losses amid high oil prices and foreign capital outflows.
NTPC made news after canceling a major ₹413 crore contract, while IT stocks faced pressure over tighter US H-1B visa rules.
The stock market is closed today for the weekend and will reopen for trading on Monday, September 21.
